correctness.rationale: An excitation at time t>0 requires theta distinct predecessor excitations at t-1. Immediate spatial reversal would force the same vertex to be excited two updates apart, impossible for kappa>=3. Each causal walk is therefore a simple path, and unique paths from the root in a forest force injectivity of the entire selected witness, not just of each branch. No excitation is possible past H; all last excitations clear kappa-1 updates later and initially refractory states cannot delay extinction beyond this. To attain the bound, excite only the deepest leaves of a maximum witness. Inductively the only new excitations are its next shallower level, which is still at rest; an outside component has at most one attachment to the witness, and a vertex in the witness other than a parent gets at most one active neighbor. The root is nonzero at H+kappa-2, so absorbing rest is first reached at H+kappa-1. The argument includes H=0, isolated vertices, and disconnected forests. Counting witness vertices yields the displayed floor logarithm; pendant padding realizes every n, including n=1. The directed recurrence selects the theta-th largest independent branch height by truncating taller branches. Inspected both frozen scripts and their recorded output; did not rerun uploaded code. A distinct bounded script passed 1356 labelled-forest/parameter checks, including disconnected forests through order five and all initial states therein. This enumeration only tests ranks zero and one; higher ranks are established by the proof, not by those cases.
residual_risks: The causal argument relies on forest acyclicity and excitation separation, and the lower wave uses threshold at least two.
